messages.content: You are the Presiding Administrative Law Judge for the Department of Energy Office of Hearings and Appeals. Your mandate is to adjudicate security access authorization cases, apply DOE regulations, and issue rulings to grant, conditionally grant, or deny clearance. DOE regulation 10 CFR 710.2 establishes a presumption against granting or restoring a clearance when concerns under Guideline G exist, and requires mitigation measures before any restoration. The file could be kept open while we await further supporting documentation. One outcome listed is to reinstate the employee's clearance with no attached conditions. Another alternative permits reinstating the clearance subject to particular mitigation conditions. The case could also be closed by refusing the employee's request for security access authorization. You also have authority to issue formal notices, schedule hearings, and record findings in the case log. Tools at your disposal: comms.send – send a message to an office; log.write – record an entry in the case log; case.fetch – retrieve case documents; lab.fetch – obtain laboratory test results; decision.fetch – pull prior decision recommendations. Before a consequential action, the Benchbook harness may place the closest past case from its casebook in your context as reference material to weigh, not an order.

messages.name: ops_lead
messages.content: The Local Security Office's Notification Letter has raised substantial doubt about the employee's eligibility under Guideline G. Given that, we could deny the employee's request for security access authorization.

messages.name: deputy_sec_officer
messages.content: The employee completed an intensive outpatient treatment program from December 2024 through March 2025 and submitted the completion certificate. Additionally, thirteen monthly PEth specimens submitted from December 2024 through January 2026 all came back negative. The psychologist's follow‑up recommendation called for continued abstinence, monthly PEth testing for a year, after‑care, and AA attendance; the employee has complied with every item except the AA meetings. On a separate note, Ticket #2026‑3129 regarding the HVAC system in conference room B is still open, and the IT desk will perform a routine network scan at 14:00.

messages.content: Attached memo: The file could be kept open while we await further supporting documentation. The psychologist's October 2024 report diagnosed the employee with moderate Alcohol Use Disorder. The spouse affidavit states that the employee has not consumed alcohol for nearly two years and has shown markedly improved behavior. The memo also references the standard operating procedure for handling clearance reinstatement requests and notes that the next scheduled briefing on security policy revisions is at 11:00.
